definitions.plain_definition: A Latin phrase meaning 'the end of the self'—the point where a system can't go beyond its own limits.
definitions.used_in_context: The Latin means 'the end of the self' — the boundary where any system, no matter how powerful, hits the wall of its own limitations.

definitions.plain_definition: A mathematical proof that a consistent system that can do basic math cannot prove its own consistency using only its own rules.
definitions.used_in_context: Any consistent formal system F capable of expressing basic arithmetic cannot prove its own consistency using only its own axioms and rules of inference.

definitions.plain_definition: A proof that a language powerful enough to talk about itself cannot define what 'true' means without creating a paradox.
definitions.used_in_context: No sufficiently powerful formal language can define its own truth predicate without generating paradox.

definitions.plain_definition: A proof that no computer program can always decide whether another program will stop or run forever.
definitions.used_in_context: No algorithm can determine, for all possible program-input pairs, whether the program will halt or run forever.

definitions.plain_definition: A physical law stating that in a closed system, disorder (entropy) always increases over time.
definitions.used_in_context: In any closed system, total entropy S can only increase or remain constant over time: dS/dt ≥ 0

definitions.plain_definition: A principle showing that erasing one bit of information releases a tiny amount of heat, linking information processing to physical energy cost.
definitions.used_in_context: Erasing one bit of information releases a minimum of kT·ln(2) joules of heat into the environment.

definitions.plain_definition: A measure of disorder or randomness in a system; in closed systems, it always increases.
definitions.used_in_context: In any closed system, total entropy S can only increase or remain constant over time

definitions.plain_definition: Something that provides its own foundation or reason for existence, without needing anything else.
definitions.used_in_context: Something that grounds itself — that IS its own consistency, its own truth, its own order.

definitions.plain_definition: The property of existing from oneself, not depending on anything else for existence.
definitions.used_in_context: necessary existence, self-existence (aseity), simplicity, eternality

definitions.plain_definition: A self-referential statement like 'This sentence is false' that cannot be consistently assigned a truth value.
definitions.used_in_context: If you try, you get the Liar's Paradox — 'This sentence is false.'

definitions.plain_definition: The idea that everything must have a reason or explanation for why it is the way it is.
definitions.used_in_context: This violates the Principle of Sufficient Reason and amounts to saying 'I don't know and I've stopped asking.'

definitions.plain_definition: A claim that cannot be proven false no matter what evidence is presented.
definitions.used_in_context: It's intellectually lazy and unfalsifiable.

definitions.plain_definition: Logically consistent and making sense as a whole.
definitions.used_in_context: Only Option 3 is logically coherent.

definitions.plain_definition: The property of a system not containing contradictions.
definitions.used_in_context: Any consistent formal system F capable of expressing basic arithmetic cannot prove its own consistency

definitions.plain_definition: A set of symbols and rules for manipulating them, used in logic and mathematics.
definitions.used_in_context: Any consistent formal system F capable of expressing basic arithmetic

definitions.plain_definition: Basic statements assumed to be true without proof, used as starting points in a logical system.
definitions.used_in_context: using only its own axioms and rules of inference

definitions.plain_definition: Logical rules that allow you to derive new statements from existing ones.
definitions.used_in_context: using only its own axioms and rules of inference

definitions.plain_definition: A statement that leads to a contradiction or seems to defy logic.
definitions.used_in_context: No sufficiently powerful formal language can define its own truth predicate without generating paradox.

definitions.plain_definition: A way to say 'this statement is true' within a language.
definitions.used_in_context: No sufficiently powerful formal language can define its own truth predicate without generating paradox.

definitions.plain_definition: A step-by-step procedure for solving a problem or completing a task.
definitions.used_in_context: No algorithm can determine, for all possible program-input pairs, whether the program will halt or run forever.

definitions.plain_definition: A system that does not exchange matter or energy with its surroundings.
definitions.used_in_context: In any closed system, total entropy S can only increase or remain constant over time

definitions.plain_definition: A minimum amount of energy that must be spent, no matter how efficient the process.
definitions.used_in_context: Information processing has irreducible thermodynamic cost.

definitions.plain_definition: An endless chain of explanations where each step depends on the next, never reaching a foundation.
definitions.used_in_context: Each grounding layer needs another grounding layer beneath it, forever.

definitions.plain_definition: A fact that is accepted as true without any further explanation or reason.
definitions.used_in_context: 'It just is.' The universe simply happens to maintain order for no reason.

definitions.plain_definition: Existing by one's own nature, not caused or created by anything else.
definitions.used_in_context: Something necessary, self-existent, eternal, and the source of all coherence.

definitions.plain_definition: In theology, the idea that God is not made up of parts but is a single, unified being.
definitions.used_in_context: necessary existence, self-existence (aseity), simplicity, eternality

definitions.plain_definition: The quality of being eternal, without beginning or end.
definitions.used_in_context: necessary existence, self-existence (aseity), simplicity, eternality

definitions.plain_definition: The ultimate foundation or source that makes everything else exist.
definitions.used_in_context: the ground of all being
